title: Netherlands – Building construction work – Verbouwing en uitbreiding IKC De Regenboog
description: De gemeente Ridderkerk heeft besloten om vernieuwbouw te realiseren voor CBS De Regenboog en incl. kinderopvang (totaal ca. 2.444 m2 BVO). De vernieuwbouw vindt plaats op de huidige locatie van CBS De Regenboog. De Opdracht betreft het door de Aannemers realiseren van de verbouwing en uitbreiding van IKC De Regenboog te Ridderkerk. De Opdracht omvat de renovatie van het bestaande gebouw (circa 1.515 m²) en de realisatie van een nieuwbouwuitbreiding van circa 1.014 m². De verbouwing en uitbreiding bestaat in grote lijnen uit: ▪ de sloopwerkzaamheden van de te slopen laagbouw; ▪ de interne sloopwerkzaamheden t.b.v. de interne verbouwing van de bestaande bouw; ▪ de realisatie van de uitbreiding; ▪ de realisatie van de interne verbouwing. De Opdracht is verdeeld in twee Percelen.

description: Hankinta koskee Laukaan seurakunnan traktorin hankintaa. Hankinta toteutetaan kansallisen kynnysarvon ylittävänä hankintana. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to negotiate and award a contract without providing for full and open competition (Including brand-name) to: Eminent Services Corp 7495 New Technology WAY Frederick, Maryland 21703 NORTH AMERICAN INDUSTRY CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM (NAICS) CODE The intended procurement is classified under NAICS code 541380 with a Size Standard $19,000,000. STATUTORY AUTHORITY This acquisition is conducted under the authority of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 13-Simplified Acquisition Procedures, Subpart 13.106-1 (b) (1), Soliciting from a single source and is not expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold. Contracts awarded using FAR Part 13-Simplified Acquisition Procedures are exempt from the requirements of FAR Part 6-Competition Requirements. GENERAL INFORMATION Title: Storage and monitoring of ManNac for FDA regulations Background Information: Under this task order, the contractor will independently provide support services to satisfy the overall operational objectives of the National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI). The refrigerated storage of the clinical grade drug-in-sachet needs to be conducted under strict temperature control and FDA-regulatory requirements. NHGRI wants to contract a company for long-term refrigerated storage of a large batch of our unlabeled investigational drug N-acetylmannosamine (ManNAc), the drug is packaged as powder-in-sachets and stored in 16 boxes (8x12x14��box dimensions) and contain 600 sachets/box. NHGRI plans to use this drug in future clinical trials of ManNAc for other indications, such as GNE-related thrombocytopenia or nephrotic disease. NHGRI anticipates storing this batch of unlabeled drug at a company for a period of up to 2 years. The refrigerated storage of the clinical grade drug-in-sachet needs to be conducted under strict temperature control and FDA-regulatory requirements. All offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) www.sam.gov. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The information received will normally be considered solely for the purposes of determining whether to proceed on a non-competitive basis or to conduct a competitive procurement. All responses must be received by November 26, 2026 at 9:00 AM Eastern time and must reference solicitation number 75N98027Q00086. Het betreft tijdelijk verblijf in een abstinente en veilige woonomgeving met herstelgerichte begeleiding voor inwoners vanaf 18 jaar die na een klinische behandeling voor verslavingsproblematiek ondersteuning nodig hebben bij hun herstel en uitstroom naar zelfstandig wonen. De tarieven worden door de aanbestedende dienst vastgesteld; gunning vindt plaats op kwaliteit. title: iWorx
description: iWorx System Required System Specifications, Minimum 18-channel data recorder with the ability to expand to additional channels. Competing systems typically provide only 2-4 channels. Ability to gang multiple recorders together for expanded data acquisition. Includes 2 channels of wireless ECG/EMG and 3-axis accelerometer capability, with expansion to 16 wired channels. Competing products generally provide only 1-2 channels. Includes an ECG simulator. Integrated Pulse Oximetry, spirometry, grip force, and intensity sensors designed for enhanced measurement accuracy. Pre-calibrated temperature, force, spirometry, and blood pressure sensors, allowing immediate use with minimal setup requirements. Two built-in low-voltage input channels (+/-15V). Built-in isolated constant current high-voltage stimulator. Must be iWire compatible, allowing future expansion and integration of additional sensors and instrumentation. Expandable to a minimum of 34 total channels. Integrated barometric pressure sensor to improve spirometry accuracy without requiring separate external hardware. Minimum 16 digital I/O channels. Minimum 1 audio output channel. Portable design capable of operation through a USB-C power connection. Includes lifetime free LabScribe software updates and an open site license. Includes unlimited online training at no additional cost.

title: 6810--501 - Dry Ice Base +4
description: Introduction: This requirement is for delivery of 600 pounds of dry ice pellets every week for a total of 52 deliveries per year (31,200 pounds per year) for a five-year period. The Government intends to solicit quotations directly from SDVOSB suppliers without discussions with offerors. Therefore, the offeror s initial offer should contain the offeror s best terms from a price and technical standpoint. However, the Government reserves the right to conduct discussions if later determined by the Contracting Officer to be necessary. The Government may reject any or all offers if such action is in the public interest; accept other than the lowest offer; and waive informalities and minor irregularities in offers received. The anticipated award date for this requirement is 12/01/2026. Background: The Cooperative Studies Program Clinical Research Pharmacy Coordinating Center s Biorepository in Albuquerque, New Mexico requires dry ice pellets for use when shipping biological samples. Required Services: A. Vendor will every week, on a Monday (unless Federal Holiday then vendor will deliver next day), deliver 600 lbs. of 5/8-inch dry ice pellets in a storage container. The storage container must keep sublimation to minimum possible level to maintain maximum useable quantity of dry ice. Acceptable performance standard is the weekly delivery of 600 pounds of dry ice pellets every week for a total of 52 deliveries per year and conformance standards are met. B. Vendor will pick up previously delivered container when delivering new container. Conformance Standards: Contract service shall ensure delivery containers meet applicable safety guidelines related to storage of dry ice. Storage container should be insulated with a hinged lid on casers designed for storage of dry ice pellets. This container is to be left at facility until the following delivery period. Container must be in good condition, fully operational casters, and lid. Container must also be free of damage or punctured insulation walls. Insulation walls of container will need to be a minimum of 2 1/2 inch thickness. Containers must have capability to hold a minimum of 700lbs of dry ice pellets. Lid must have a mechanism for holding the lid closed and in place. Containers must have a minimum of four casters, two that swivel, to support total weight of at least 700lbs of dry ice and allow for mobility across flat level surfaces. Loss due to sublimination should be less than eight percent (8%) of total mass every 24 hours. Common rule is 3-8% of total mass every 24 hours. Greater loss would be a result of inadequate or damaged containers. Hours of Coverage: Normal delivery hours are Monday through Friday from 7:30 am to 3:00 pm Mountain time. Deliveries must occur during normal delivery hours. Federal Holidays observed by NMVAHCS are: New Years' Day Labor Day Martin Luther King Day Columbus Day Presidents' Day Veterans' Day Memorial Day Thanksgiving Day Juneteenth Christmas Day Independence Day Other Pertinent Information or Special Considerations: Delivery Address/Point of Contact: Department of Veterans Affairs Cooperative Studies Program Clinical Research Pharmacy Coordinating Center 2401 Centre Ave SE Albuquerque, NM 87106 Points of Contact and Delivery Verification Steven Micklos, steven.micklos@va.gov, 505-265-1711 x6344 Paul Hicks, paul.hicks@va.gov, (505) 248-3206 We have our own free-standing facility detached from VA Hospital with loading/receiving dock. There is not a max radius location from vendor to delivery location as long as the integrity of the dry ice supply is not compromised in transit. Delivery Hours: 8:00am-3:30pm (MT) Delayed Orders: Delayed orders are not acceptable. Analyzing and testing biospecimens cannot be conducted as there would be no means to transport biospecimens while remaining viable for testing. Period of Performance: The period of performance shall be for one base year PLUS up to four (4) option years. The Government may extend the term of the awarded base/option year by written notice to the Contractor within 30 days of annual expiration date, provided that the Government gives the Contractor a preliminary written notice of its intent to extend at least 60 days before the contract expires. The preliminary (>60 day) notice does not commit the Government to an extension BASE YEAR CLIN Description QTY Unit 0001 Dry Ice Pellets 31,200 LB NOTE: CLIN is delivered in 52 separate deliveries (600 LB per delivery every week) OPTION YEAR 1 CLIN Description QTY Unit 1001 Dry Ice Pellets 31,200 LB OPTION YEAR 2 CLIN Description QTY Unit 2001 Dry Ice Pellets 31,200 LB OPTION YEAR 3 CLIN Description QTY Unit 3001 Dry Ice Pellets 31,200 LB OPTION YEAR 4 CLIN Description QTY Unit 4001 Dry Ice Pellets 31,200 LB

title: Construction Services for Confined Aquatic Disposal Cell Construction and Maintenance Dredging of the Providence River Federal Navigation Project, Providence, Rhode Island.
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing a Sources Sought Announcement for the upcoming dredging project located in Providence, Rhode Island. This announcement is to determine the interest, availability and capability of Small and Large Business concerns as described below. The NAICS code for this procurement is 237990. The solicitation for this project is anticipated to be issued on or about 15 March 2027. The construction will begin in September 2027 and is expected to take approximately 2 years to complete. The estimated construction cost is between $80,000,000 and $100,000,000. The Providence River Maintenance Dredging project involves two major sequences of dredging and disposal activities. The first work sequence will be the construction of a new Confined Aquatic Disposal (CAD) cell adjacent to the Providence River. The second work sequence under this contract will include maintenance dredging of the Providence River and Harbor Federal Navigation Project (FNP) to its authorized depths and dimensions. The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 5,500,000 cubic yards (cy) of material using closed clamshell buckets for both major sequences of work over the course of two years. The new CAD cell will be in the Edgewood Basin area located adjacent to the Providence FNP (hereafter the �Edgewood Shoals North (ESN) CAD cell�). To access the CAD cell area, an access channel will be dug between the Providence FNP and the CAD cell area. The access channel will be approximately 100 ft wide and -25 MLLW deep. The CAD cell will have surface dimensions of approximately 1000 ft. by 1000 ft. and be dug to a depth of -60 MLLW. The material excavated to build the access channel is generally a mix of sandy silt and shell fragments. Within the CAD cell area the material is generally described as soft grey to black organic silt with some layers of firm sandy silt and some shell fragments and coarse-grained material. Material excavated from the access channel and CAD cell area will be placed at four locations: Port Edgewood Basin, the Fox Point Reach CAD cells, Prudence Island Disposal Site, and the Rhode Island Sound Disposal Site. This work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,200,000 cy to construct thew ESN CAD cell and its access channel, which must be completed before maintenance dredging of the FNP can begin. The maintenance dredging proposed work consists of mechanically dredging the Providence River FNP to the full -40 MLLW depth plus 2-feet of allowable overdepth. 2,300,000 cy (1,200,000 cy required depth, with up to 1,100,000 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting generally of poorly graded medium to fine sand with silt. The dredge material from this maintenance portion of work will be placed in the ESN CAD cell. Environmental coordination and permitting is being completed by the U.S. Army of Engineers, New England District. All dredging and disposal activities for this project have prescribed work windows that incorporate environmental and recreational time of year restrictions. Refer to the Draft Specification Section provided with this announcement for specifics on the time of year work restrictions. In order to accomplish all dredging requirements within the specified dredging window it is expected that the Contractor will need to meet a production rate of 300,000 CY per 30 calendar days. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is requesting responses to the questions below from both small and large businesses[MC1] . Draft drawings showing a concept design plan and draft Specification Section of 01 11 00 SUMMARY OF WORK have been provided with this announcement to help provide more context for the contract work and responses to these questions. Considering the different disposal locations, are there suggestions on a bid structure that will provide for the most accurate costs of different disposal locations? Any draft restrictions that may impact dredging and/or disposal operations? Any concerns on the period of performance of September 2027 to September 2029 considering the environmental windows and amount of work? If so, why? Any comments about the bed leveling planned in the Fox Point Reach? Are there concerns about this part of the plan, if so, why? Interested firms should also demonstrate their project experience, by providing two (2) projects within the last ten years, which meet the following requirements: Dredging by mechanical means demonstrating a minimum production rate of 300,000 cubic yards in one consecutive 30-day period. Experience with placement of dredged material at an open water placement site in New England during the fall/winter months of October through March. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, etc.), type of equipment the firm is proposing to use on the project, and two (2) example projects performed by the firm in the last ten (10) years (including Points of Contact for those projects) showing experience with the proposed equipment at the production rate listed above. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications meeting the same qualifications listed above, which will be used to support the bidder's effort. Firms may use subcontractor experience to demonstrate experience with the requirements, but the role and work performed by each team member (prime and subcontractors) on projects demonstrating that team member's experience shall be the same as the role for that team member for this project. Bid bond will need to be provided with the bid. Responses are limited to twenty pages and due by November 26 , 2026. Responses should be addressed to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District, 696 Virginia Road, Concord, MA 01742-2751, ATTN: Kyle Hall, or electronically to Kyle.K.Hall@usace.army.mil. title: J065--Notice of Intent to Sole Source Rauland Nurse Call System Services
description: This is a Special Notice for commercial items prepared in accordance with FAR Subpart 5.2, Synopsis of Proposed Contract Actions. This announcement constitutes the only Notice of Intent (NOI) to Sole Source (SS) and synopsis of proposed action. The Department of Veterans Affairs Michael E. DeBakey VA Medical Center (MEDVAMC) Network Contracting Office (NCO) 16 intends to issue and award a Sole Source single award Firm-Fixed Price type contract delivery order IAW FAR Overhaul Part 12 with a performance period of one (1) Base Year and four (4) Option Years to Lone Star Communications, Inc. located at 1414 Post N Paddock St, Grand Prairie, TX to furnish all software, tools, and licenses for a VA owned Rauland Responder 5 Nurse Call System, located at MEDVAMC 2002 Holcombe Boulevard, Houston, TX 77030. It has been determined that through initial Market Research, only 1 (one) Rauland authorized vendor exists to perform the required services in the Houston, TX area. The contract will be a Firm Fixed Price single award. The statutory authority for this non-competitive acquisition as implemented by FAR 6.302- Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements . The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 811210 Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance, with a small business size standard of $34M, and the FSC/PSC is J065 Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment Medical, Dental, and Veterinary Equipment and Supplies. Services to be awarded are shown below. Rauland Enterprise Software Licenses (Quantity #709) Customer Care Visits (Quantity #4) Annual T upgrades (Quantity #1) ESA Hardware/Support (Quantity #1) The contractor shall provide and ensure safe, secure, and careful handling and delivery of results in accordance with established guidelines from the Department of Veterans Affairs Handbook 6500 and drafted statement of work. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS. A SOLICITATION WILL NOT BE POSTED. Telephone requests will not be honored. No award will be made based on quotes or offers received in response to this notice. All responsible sources may identify their interest to meet this requirement to Contract Specialist and date identified on page one of this announcement. Additionally, any response to this notice must show clear, compelling and convincing evidence that competition will be advantageous to the government by providing the following: 1.Business Size and Socio-Economic Status: (a) Indicate whether your business is large or small (b) If small, indicate if your firm qualifies as a small, emerging business, or small disadvantaged business (c) If disadvantaged, specify under which disadvantaged group and if your firm is certified under Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act (d) Indicate if your firm is a certified Hub zone firm (e) Indicate if your firm is a woman-owned or operated business (f) Indicate if your firm is a VIP verified Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) (g) Include the DUNS number of your firm. (h) State whether your firm is registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) at www.sam.gov and/or the SBA VetCerts Registry at https://veterans.certify.sba.gov/. If not, please NOTE: any future solicitation could only be awarded to a contractor who is registered in SAM. To receive award based on VOSB or SDVOSB status you must be registered in the SBA VetCerts Registry. The intent of this notice is for informational purposes only. Interested parties may submit information for consideration by the government to: robert.arabie@va.gov no later than the response due date/time identified above. All responses received by the closing date specified herein will be considered by the Government, any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that the responding company can provide the same services by the required date. However, a determination by the Government to not compete is solely within the discretion of the Government. Thank you.

title: Rakennusurakointitöiden puitehankinta vuosille 2027-2029
description: Rakennusurakointitöiden puitehankinta vuosille 2027-2029 Naantalin kaupungin yksiköt (Tilaaja) pyytää tarjouksia rakennusurakointitöiden toteuttamisesta sopimuskaudelle. Hankinnan kohteena olevat työt toteutetaan joko erikseen minikilpailutettavina toimeksiantoina tai suoraan hankittavina töinä sopimusehtojen mukaisesti. Rakennusurakoita kilpailutetaan lisäksi kohdekohtaisilla urakkakilpailulla. Sopimuskauden arvioitu alkamisajankohta on 1.1.2027. Lisäksi Tilaaja varaa mahdollisuuden kahteen optiovuoteen (1+1). Optiolla tarkoitetaan mahdollisuutta sopimuksen jatkamiseen alkuperäisin ehdoin. Tilaaja päättää optioiden käytöstä erikseen. Hankinta tullaan toteuttamaan puitejärjestelynä. Tilattavien töiden sisältö ja määrä eivät ole ennalta tiedossa eikä Tilaaja sitoudu mihinkään hankintamääriin sopimuskauden aikana. Pienurakat voivat sisältää rakennus-, maalaus-, matto-, tasoite-, vedeneristys- sekä laatoitus- ja teräsrakennetöitä. Urakat toteutetaan noudattaen rakennusalan yleisiä sopimusehtoja YSE 1998.,

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Planungsleistungen für ein Nahwärmenetz der Leistungsphasen 2 – 4 in den Quartieren Gildekamp und Gotthunkamp in der Stadt Röbel/Müritz.
description: Die Stadt Röbel/Müritz erwägt den Neubau eines innovativen Nahwärmenetzes in den Quartieren Gildekamp und Gotthunskamp mit Potential zur Erweiterung und damit zum Anschluss anderer Quartiere der Stadt. Das Ziel ist der Aufbau einer zukunftssicheren, CO2-mindernden und wirtschaftlichen Wärmeversorgung der Stadt Röbel/Müritz in Teilabschnitten bis 2045. Dabei sind die Anforderungen, die sich aus dem Wärmeplanungsgesetz vom 20.12.2023 § 30 Abs. 1 und § 31 Abs. 1 ergeben einzuhalten. Gegenstand der zu vergebenden Leistung ist die Erbringung der stufenweisen Planungsleistungen gemäß § 53 der Leistungsphasen 2 bis 4 HOAI (Vorplanung, Entwurfsplanung, Genehmigungsplanung) für das Nahwärmenetz Röbel, unter Beachtung der Anforderungen der BEW-Förderrichtlinie (Fassung vom 16. Dezember 2025). Die Leistungen müssen die im BAFA-Merkblatt („Bundesförderung für effiziente Wärmenetze – Merkblatt Antragstellung, technische Anforderungen und Verwendungsnachweis) definierten Mindestinhalte nach Ziffer 4.2.3 vollständig abdecken.

title: RFI Process control system plumbing and programming
description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the US Army DEVCOM Soldier Center to identify potential sources to provide expert engineering support to trouble shoot process control system providing steam water and air. Must have expertise in process control plumbing and control valves for steam systems. Must have expertise in Allen Bradley PLC programming. The Government requests that responses be submitted electronically to mary.k.prebensen.civ@army.mil and Wesley.s.shaw.civ@army.mil by November 26th, 2026 by 5pm EST. Background: The Government (DEVCOM Soldier Center) is in need of expert engineering support to diagnose current PLC and piping system which support multiple hydraulic press systems. The existing system controls water, steam and air to molding tooling, and the PLC operates on custom Allen-Bradley control software. As it stands, the system is physically installed, however does not provide necessary temperature control in either manual or automatic modes. Issues may be traced to the original system design, pipe rack installation, PLC programming or some combination of the three. Description: Expert engineering services are sought to diagnose newly installed PLC control system to ensure that it can meet system design requirements, can be operated safely and reliably, and is adaptable for future operation and changing requirements. A new PLC system has been designed and installed per a list of system requirements, however is not able to control temperature per design requirements either due to control logic, poor valve selection or related piping design/installation. SC requires a 3rd party engineering service to validate as-built drawings against the installed system, verify/update PLC programming, provide necessary hardware changes to bring the system up to full operability. Specific System Specifications: Electric steam boiler provides 125psi dry steam as primary heat source for molding tooling. Standalone chiller provides chilled water at ~60 psi, and house air provides air for purge and mist functions. The Allen-Bradley PLC system controls the various media through a series of modulating valves to heat or cool the tooling. The PLC is intended to have recipe writing and management for automated control. Basic recipe for our process includes steam heat via pressure control to desired temperature setpoint, hold for ~1 hr while controlling temperature. The tooling is then cooled with chilled water at a controlled cooling rate. Our standard tooling includes an upper and lower platen, and the PLC has capability to control these independently. Additional system requirements will be included if there is a future RFP. Current known system issues: System will not maintain equivalent temperature for upper and lower platens during heat up or hold. System will not control cooling rate based on system feedback loop. System trend screen not displaying data correctly. System alarms remain untested. Mist function does not function without vibration of piping rack. Unique Vendor qualifications: Potential vendor must be US based and employ US citizens identified to work on the PLC system due to sensitivity of materials and products produced by the installation laboratory. Potential vendor must be licensed in process system design with specific expertise in steam controls. Potential vendor must be able to read modify and update Allen Bradly system code. Deliverables: Full system walkdown and comparison to As-built drawings. Analysis of system design, layout, valve selection, PLC operability as compared to provided list of system requirements. List of proposed design changes to meet system requirements and cost of implementation. Install required hardware and make required changes to system software. May subcontract for implementation of hardware changes. Provide updated As-built drawings for plumbing systems, electrical systems, PLC controls systems. System demonstration and verification to the As-built drawings provided Modified code in digital and hardcopy. Verified system manual. Full system demonstration and minimum 1 day training on system operation. Delivery Date: Government estimates work will be completed within 6 months of date of contract award. Government Furnished Property (Equipment/Materials/Information/Computer Utilization): All work to be performed on site at SC with access to existing PLC and piping rack. description: Outdoor Fitness Facility, Building 389� Supply, Delivery, and Limited Installation Support Notice Type: Sources Sought / Market Research Notice Number: HARBSS-2027-01 Contracting Office: 482d CONF/PK Location of Performance: Homestead Air Reserve Base, Florida Response Due Date/Time: November 26, 2026, 5:00 PM EST Response Submission: Nika Salemi, nika.salemi.2@us.af.mil Proposed NAICS Code: 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Proposed Product Service Code (PSC): 5670 Building Components, Prefabricated 1. Notice Purpose THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ISSUED FOR MARKET-RESEARCH AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A SOLICITATION, REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, REQUEST FOR QUOTATION, INVITATION FOR BID, OR COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT TO AWARD A CONTRACT. The 482d Contracting Flight, Homestead Air Reserve Base (HARB), FL, seeks information from capable commercial sources, including all small-business socioeconomic categories, to determine the availability and capability of firms that can perform the requirement described in Attachment 1 KYJM19-9003 Outdoor Fitness SOW, Red Horse Project, 12 Nov 2026. Responses will be used to support acquisition planning, including consideration of the appropriate contract type, acquisition approach, and potential small-business set-aside strategy. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparation or submission of information in response to this notice. A response to this notice is not required to respond to a future solicitation, if issued. Any future solicitation will be announced separately. 2. Requirement Overview The 482d Contracting Flight, Homestead Air Reserve Base (HARB), FL is conducting market research for the Outdoor Fitness Facility, Building 389 project at Homestead Air Reserve Base (HARB), Florida. The anticipated requirement is primarily for the procurement, delivery, and associated submittals for construction materials and equipment required to support construction of an outdoor fitness facility. Air Force RED HORSE personnel will perform the majority of construction and installation activities. Contractor installation responsibilities are limited principally to the steel picket fence and, if applicable, a separate lightning-protection system. The contractor would be expected to: Procure and deliver all materials identified in the Government-furnished bill of materials (BOM), Attachment 2 Outdoor Fitness Facility, BOM Template. Furnish the Pre-Engineered Building (PEB) package, including engineered shop drawings and all associated structure materials. Coordinate concrete-truck deliveries to support Government construction execution. Furnish the specified construction equipment for the required durations, fueled and ready for operation at the work site. Install a new steel picket fence, including site restoration for areas disturbed by fence installation. Install a lightning-protection system if the proposed PEB cannot include a compliant built-in lightning-protection system. The provided BOM identifies, among other materials and equipment, rubber fitness flooring, concrete masonry materials, electrical distribution materials, outdoor fans, motion-activated lighting, concrete, base course, PEB-related items, and construction-equipment rentals. 3. Anticipated Scope 3.1 Material Procurement and Delivery The contractor shall be capable of procuring, delivering, and warranting the materials and equipment identified in the Government-furnished BOM. The contractor shall provide required material and equipment submittals before ordering materials, and the Government will approve final submittals in writing before purchase. Anticipated submittals include: Steel picket fence; PEB signed and sealed shop drawings; Outdoor ceiling fans; Lighting; Smart meter; Electrical panel; Fitness flooring; Bird netting; Material warranty plan, including roof, flooring, and other applicable equipment warranties; and Fence material and labor warranty. 3.2 Pre-Engineered Building Package The contractor shall be capable of providing a complete PEB material package based on Government design drawings, including digitally signed and sealed shop drawings prepared by a Professional Engineer. The PEB package is expected to include, at a minimum: Lifting-rack/support beams; A fixed steel beam with predrilled holes for 25-foot ropes; Toe-hold bars located three inches above the finished floor; Factory coating and painting, with Government-selected colors; Medium-bronze exterior roof panels and manufacturer-standard light interior roof panels; Standing seam metal roofing; Gutters and downspouts; Built-in copper lightning protection, where available; and Black, heavy-duty polyethylene bird netting with �-inch mesh meeting or exceeding the specified mesh-quality and break-strength requirements. The PEB shall be designed in accordance with the SOW�s specified structural and high-velocity-wind requirements. The SOW requires a minimum 20-year material warranty, a current Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance for the PEB and insulation, and a roof assembly capable of the stated uplift and wind criteria. Zinc-plated metal is prohibited. 3.3 Lightning Protection System � Conditional Installation If a compliant PEB with built-in lightning protection is unavailable, the contractor shall be capable of furnishing and installing a conventional lightning-protection and grounding system following completion of RED HORSE construction activities. The contractor�s capability should include: Copper lightning-protection materials; Installation shop drawings; UL-listed and labeled components; Fence-bonding connections; Grounding-system testing and test-point documentation; Third-party inspection and written certification by an entity independent of the system designer and installer; and Compliance with the project�s cited lightning-protection requirements. 3.4 Steel Picket Fence Installation and Site Restoration The contractor shall be capable of furnishing and installing a steel picket fence around the outdoor-fitness-facility overhang structure. The fence must be located at least five feet from the roof overhang and include an accessible, lockable gate/door. The fence-related scope includes required access and equipment doors, hardware, and restoration of disturbed areas using St. Augustine sod. 3.5 Construction Equipment The contractor shall be capable of furnishing the construction equipment identified in the BOM for the stated rental periods or project duration. Anticipated equipment includes a 12,000-pound telehandler forklift, skid loaders with buckets and forks, a water truck, scissor lifts, straight-track manlifts, a double-drum roller, a mini excavator with hammer, a dump truck, and concrete forms with pins. Equipment shall be delivered to the project site, fueled, and ready for operation. The contractor will not be responsible for subsequent refueling unless otherwise established in a future solicitation. 3.6 Installation Access and On-Site Requirements Potential sources should be capable of working on an active military installation and complying with applicable installation access, identification, safety, security, and operations-security requirements. For contractor-performed installation work, the contractor must be capable of providing an English-fluent site superintendent who remains on site during contract performance. Excavation, if required, will require coordination and permits before work begins; the SOW specifies that permit requests must be submitted at least three weeks before excavation. Normal anticipated work hours for fence installation are 0730�1630, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays, unless alternate hours are approved in writing. 4. description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the US Army DEVCOM Soldier Center to identify potential sources to provide expert engineering support to trouble shoot process control system providing steam water and air. Must have expertise in process control plumbing and control valves for steam systems. Must have expertise in Allen Bradley PLC programming. The Government requests that responses be submitted electronically to mary.k.prebensen.civ@army.mil and Wesley.s.shaw.civ@army.mil by November 26th, 2026 by 5pm EST. Background: The Government (DEVCOM Soldier Center) is in need of expert engineering support to diagnose current PLC and piping system which support multiple hydraulic press systems. The existing system controls water, steam and air to molding tooling, and the PLC operates on custom Allen-Bradley control software. As it stands, the system is physically installed, however does not provide necessary temperature control in either manual or automatic modes. Issues may be traced to the original system design, pipe rack installation, PLC programming or some combination of the three. Description: Expert engineering services are sought to diagnose newly installed PLC control system to ensure that it can meet system design requirements, can be operated safely and reliably, and is adaptable for future operation and changing requirements. A new PLC system has been designed and installed per a list of system requirements, however is not able to control temperature per design requirements either due to control logic, poor valve selection or related piping design/installation. SC requires a 3rd party engineering service to validate as-built drawings against the installed system, verify/update PLC programming, provide necessary hardware changes to bring the system up to full operability. Standalone chiller provides chilled water at ~60 psi, and house air provides air for purge and mist functions. The PLC is intended to have recipe writing and management for automated control. Basic recipe for our process includes steam heat via pressure control to desired temperature setpoint, hold for ~1 hr while controlling temperature. The tooling is then cooled with chilled water at a controlled cooling rate. Our standard tooling includes an upper and lower platen, and the PLC has capability to control these independently. title: Denmark – Road transport services – Udbud af Kontrakt vedrørende transport og distribution for Statens Serum Institut i Danmark (1)
description: Statens Serum Institut (SSI) er et institut under Sundheds- og Kirkeministeriet, hvis mission er, forebygge og bekæmpe infektionssygdomme og medfødte sygdomme gennem forskning, overvågning, diagnostik og rådgivning. SSI har i den forbindelse behov for en række transportydelser i Danmark herunder: • Distribution til SSI’s nationale kunder • Afhentning af patientprøver på hospitaler • Afhentning af spildevandsprøver • Option vedrørende en Beredskabssituation.…. Transportopgaverne omfatter kølegods og andet gods. Ydelsen omfatter transport i hele Danmark, herunder Bornholm og ikke-brofaste øer. Alt arbejde under kontrakten skal udføres i overensstemmelse med alle til enhver tid gældende love, forordninger, standarder og bekendtgørelser om kvalitet og kvalitetssikring inden for det relevante fagområde, herunder • Vejledning af 5. november 2013 i god distributionspraksis for humanmedicinske lægemidler EØS(europa.eu), og • Transport af farligt gods

description: Het doel van deze inkoop is het contracteren van een opdrachtnemer voor de realisatie van een drainage-, verzamelleiding- en lozingssysteem in het gebied Perkpolder. Met deze maatregelen wordt grondwater afkomstig uit de omgeving van de waterkering gecontroleerd afgevangen en afgevoerd naar de Westerschelde. De werkzaamheden dragen bij aan het voorkomen van een mogelijke negatieve invloed op de grond- en oppervlaktewaterkwaliteit in het achterland als gevolg van mogelijke uitloging vanuit de in de waterkering toegepaste thermisch gereinigde grond (TGG). Zie het reeds ingevulde veld m.b.t. korte omschrijving.

title: Germany – Construction-site supervision services – RV Baubegleitendens Qualitätscontrolling
description: Gegenstand dieser Rahmenvereinbarung sind Dienstleistungen des baubegleitenden sachverständigen Qualitätscontrollings bei Hochbauprojekten (Neubau, Umbau sowie serielle bzw. modulare Bauweise). Die Leistungen beziehen sich auf Hochbauprojekte im Berliner Raum, insbesondere im Segment: - Seniorenwohnungen, - Studentenwohnungen, - Beschäftigtenwohnungen, - sowie ergänzend Gewerbeflächen und Kindertagesstätten (Kitas). Die Leistungen erfolgen in Form stichprobenartiger, unabhängiger Qualitätsprüfungen während der Bauausführung beginnend ab der Bodenplatte bzw. Gründung bis zur Übergabe des Gebäudes mit dem Ziel der Sicherstellung der Ausführungsqualität, der frühzeitigen Erkennung von Mängeln sowie der Reduzierung von Mängeln zum Zeitpunkt der Abnahme.
